thread:
oncall-bot: ALERT P1: gpu-node-pool autoscaler failing; queues growing in eu-central-1 inference cluster. Paging oncall. :rotating_light:

Ravi K: I'm taking pager. Seeing steady queue increase. p95 latency jumped from 120ms -> 9.1s in ~8m. frontend 502/504 counts rising.

Sofia L: which pool?

Ravi K: inference-eu-pool. Autoscaler logs show nodes requested but pods still pending. Looks like scheduling failures related to MIG capacities.

Eve M: any customer reports?

customer-success: Two enterprise customers (acct-440, acct-999) reported failed long-poll in the last 10m. Tickets opened.

Ravi K: grabbing autoscaler log snippet:
```
I0304 03:14:02 cluster-autoscaler: ScaleUp: had 30 unschedulable pods, trying to find nodes
I0304 03:14:03 cluster-autoscaler: candidates: [nodepool-eu-runner-1, nodepool-eu-runner-2]
E0304 03:14:04 cluster-autoscaler: NoCapacity: failed to launch nodes: ProviderError: InsufficientCapacity; also scheduling failures: MIG_FRAGMENTATION, RequestedSingleGpuButNodeHasMultipleSlices
```

Sofia L: ProviderInsufficientCapacity means spot/preemptible requests were also attempted and denied. But autoscaler should still try on-demand. Why not?

infra-bot: pool-config for inference-eu-pool: MIG profile toggled: mix of 1x40g and 4x10g across image versions. image-tag: gpu-experiment-2026-02 (unrolled partially).

Ravi K: That matches what I'm seeing on nodes: some nodes have 4x10g MIG slices, others are 1x40g. Our large-model pods request a contiguous 40g allocation. Binpack algorithm can't combine slices and treats fragmented free slices as unusable for single-pod 40g. So capacity exists in aggregate but is stranded. Autoscaler opportunistically asked for more spot machines first and got InsufficientCapacity, then retried but with same experimental image so new nodes also have fragmented GPUs.

Eve M: can we move workloads to the nodes that are unpartitioned? Node affinity or explicit scheduling?

Ravi K: yes, plan in two phases: immediate mitigation to reduce customer impact, then remediation. Proposed immediate steps:
- Apply admission rate limit on non-enterprise routes (throttle)
- Evict best-effort batch jobs to free contiguous GPUs on some nodes
- Taint unpartitioned nodes and prefer schedule critical pods to them (node affinity patch)
- Request emergency on-demand capacity with standard image (no MIG partitions)

Sofia L: avoid mass evictions that could cause cascading restarts. Evict only labeled batch/low-priority. I'll craft a drain/evict command for those labels.

Ravi K: executing throttle rule now (edge gateway):
```
# edge rate limit for non-enterprise
curl -X POST https://edge.internal/api/rl -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","rate_per_min":40}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

infra-bot: rate-limit rule applied, new non-SLA RPS reduced ~55%.

Ravi K: evicting jobs with label workload=best-effort (rolling):
```
kubectl get pods -l workload=best-effort -n inference -o name | xargs -n1 -P4 kubectl delete -n inference --grace-period=30
```

Sofia L: deleting pods; we're seeing some freed whole GPUs on nodepool-eu-runner-3. Scheduling starting to place 40g pods there. Queue dropping slowly.

Ravi K: also submitted on-demand request with standard image: request-id od-44321, +3 nodes of type g5.12xlarge (no MIG partitions). ETA ~7m.

infra-bot: request od-44321 accepted; two nodes will be spot/one on-demand due to regional constraints.

Eve M: while new nodes come up, can we fallback small-model route for large batch requests? That would reduce GPU pressure quickly.

Ravi K: yes, we've toggled routing so heavy-batch endpoint points to rwd-lite-1 (quantized) for non-enterprise. Enterprise stays routed to their SLA routes.

customer-success: notifying affected enterprise customers about degraded performance and that we're prioritizing SLA traffic.

Sofia L: kube describe on a persistently pending pod (infer-large-qp-23):
```
Name: infer-large-qp-23
Status: Pending
Events:
  Type    Reason                 Age   From               Message
  ----    ------                 ----  ----               -------
  Warning FailedScheduling       21s   kube-scheduler     0/12 nodes are available: 8 InsufficientGPUMemory, 4 Node had no matching MIG profile.
```

Ravi K: note the "Node had no matching MIG profile" - scheduler sees node slices that don't match requested resource shape. It's why pods stay pending even if a node has enough aggregate memory.

Eve M: new nodes registered (od-44321-01..03). Scheduling happened, several pending pods moved onto them. Observed queue fall: 230 -> 58 in 9m. 5xx rates down.

Sofia L: after some pods scheduled, p95 latency back to ~1.9s. Enterprise customers still experiencing intermittent timeouts for long-poll but most requests are now served.

Ravi K: immediate summary for post-incident notes:
- Root cause: partial rollout of MIG partition experiment left mixed MIG profiles across pool; pods requesting a contiguous 40g GPU couldn't be scheduled onto fragmented nodes. Autoscaler attempted scale but requested additional nodes with same experimental image and hit provider capacity for spot instances, delaying recovery. Stranded GPU slices caused queue growth and customer-impacting errors.
- Mitigations performed: throttle non-SLA, evicted best-effort batch jobs, tainted/un-tainted nodes to prefer unpartitioned nodes, requested on-demand unpartitioned nodes, routed heavy traffic to quantized fallback for non-SLA, customer notifications.
- Impact: two enterprise customers saw degraded performance and some failed long-polls ~8-12m window. No data loss.

Eve M: handoff: I'm taking lead for remediation changes. Ravi, if you could keep watch for the next 30m, I'll start remediation tasks.

Ravi K: will monitor. also will prepare a short incident blurb for status page.

Sofia L: remediation items to add to postmortem and infra backlog:
- Rollback/complete the MIG experiment and reimage the partially rolled nodes to unified standard image
- Add autoscaler logic to detect MIG fragmentation and either prefer unpartitioned nodes or change request shape
- Add admission controller to reject pod specs that require contiguous GPU sizes not available in cluster (fail fast)
- Create CI gate: disallow partial rollouts that change MIG profiles without a canary policy and auto-rollback
- Improve cloud fallback: prefer on-demand after spot failures for critical pools

customer-success: posting update to customers: "We applied mitigations; traffic restored with degraded performance for a short period. We'll follow up with root cause and timeline."

oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations in place, queue trending down, severity may be lowered to P2 once stable for 20m.

Eve M: scheduling a follow-up postmortem meeting. I'll own the remediation epic.

Ravi K: handing pager to Sofia for night shift in 15m. I'll remain on-call for 1hr for follow-ups.

Sofia L: ack. thanks team.
